q: What is the main purpose of continuous integration (CI) for a data engineering team?
o: Deploy every commit to production immediately
Merge changes frequently and validate them automatically with tests
Back up notebooks every night
Run all jobs continuously
e: CI means integrating changes often and running automated checks (lint, unit tests, validation) on every change. Continuous deployment then releases the validated code.

q: Which is the best way to make a PySpark transformation unit-testable?
o: Keep it in one long notebook cell
Write it as a function that takes and returns a DataFrame, in a separate module
Read the source table inside the function using a hard-coded name
Test it by running the production job
e: Pure DataFrame-in, DataFrame-out functions in modules can be imported by notebooks and jobs, and tested on small in-memory data with pytest.

q: Which utility compares two DataFrames for both schema and rows in a unit test, ignoring row order by default?
o: `df1.collect() == df2.collect()`
`assertDataFrameEqual(actual, expected)`
`df1.exceptAll(df2).count() == 0`
`assertSchemaEqual(actual, expected)`
e: pyspark.testing.assertDataFrameEqual checks schema and data, ignoring row order by default. assertSchemaEqual checks only the schema.

q: Two engineers change the same pipeline at the same time. Which workflow keeps this safe?
o: Both edit the same shared Git folder on main
Each works on a feature branch in their own Git folder and merges through a pull request
One exports the notebook as DBC and emails it
Use notebook revision history to undo conflicts
e: Feature branches in personal Git folders and reviewed pull requests isolate changes and make conflicts visible before merging.

q: The same job must be deployed to dev, test and prod with a different catalog in each. What is the recommended approach?
o: Create the job by hand in each workspace
Copy the job JSON and edit it per environment
Define it once in a bundle and use targets with variables
Hard-code the catalog and change it before each deployment
e: A bundle describes the job once. Targets and variables supply the environment-specific values, and `databricks bundle deploy -t <target>` promotes it.
